 While the Social Security Administration has already decided the adjustments that recipients will get in 2027, an advocacy group for older Americans is petitioning Congress to issue stimulus checks to make up for expected financial shortfalls.
 The Senior Citizens League (TSCL) is calling on the incoming Congressional body to make several changes for Social Security recipients, including a one-time $1,400 check to senior citizens to make up for what the group calls “inadequate” cost of living adjustments (COLAs) and rising inflation.

 The group is also asking the now-Democratic majority in the House and Senate to add dental, vision and hearing care to Medicare, restore budget cuts to Medicare and Medicaid that were made in the most recent budget bill (aka the “One Big Beautiful Bill”) and to lift or eliminate the Social Security Payroll tax threshold, which would widen the pool of people paying into Social Security.

 “Ensuring Americans can retire with dignity isn’t a left-wing issue or a right-wing issue; it’s not a Democratic issue or a Republican issue. It affects all of us, and all of us stand to lose if Congress fails to act to protect America’s seniors,” said TSCL Executive Director Shannon Benton in a statement.
 A flat COLA
 Soaring gas and food prices, along with increased healthcare costs, have put many older Americans in an uncomfortable financial position. While Social Security benefits for recipients will increase 3.6% in 2027, an average of about $75 per month, that’s noticeably below the 4% increase in the consumer price index year to date. It also doesn’t account for the higher number of doctor visits seniors often face. Add in the fact that one in five Americans over the age of 50 have no retirement savings and the financial security crisis leans more toward the redline.
 The 3.6% increase that will take place next year is hardly the smallest on record. Benefits remained unchanged in 2009 and 2010 . But it’s also far from the biggest increase. Social Security recipients saw a 14.3% increase in 1980 as the global recession took hold.
 The 2027 COLA will work out to an even lower increase, since Medicare costs are increasing. Some recipients will only see an extra $65.50 per month.

 The unretirement predicament
 Seniors are the country’s fastest-growing homeless population, said TSCL. And a growing number of people who retired years ago are finding they need to return to work to pay bills and daily necessities.
 A February study by AARP found that 7% of retirees had unretired in the previous six months. For people 50 and older who are looking for work, AARP says 41% report they are doing so because they cannot afford everyday living costs. And, making matters worse, roughly one-quarter of those older workers say they’re worried about losing their job in the next year.
 Of people in Georgia over the age of 65, 12.1% live below the poverty line , which is worse than the national average of 11.3%. And some 8.5% of people 60 years old or older are affected by food insecurity.
